name: Gothic
description: Vertical-emphasis ecclesiastical style defined by pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses that transfer outward thrust so walls can dissolve into stained glass. Aspires to height as a theological metaphor for heaven.

name: Romanesque
description: Pre-Gothic monastic style with massive stone walls, round arches, barrel vaults and small windows. Fortress-like, weighty, horizontal in emphasis.

name: Byzantine
description: Central-plan style built around a great dome on pendentives, golden mosaics, and tightly integrated interior volumes. Hagia Sophia is the paradigm.

name: Baroque
description: Dramatic, theatrical Counter-Reformation style with curvilinear plans, deep moldings, concave/convex facades, dynamic lighting, and integrated painting and sculpture.

name: Neoclassical
description: Revival of Greco-Roman form: symmetry, columnar porticoes, clean proportions rooted in the classical orders. Civic buildings, libraries, courthouses.

name: Art Deco
description: Streamlined geometric ornament, metallic materials, stepped setbacks, zigzag motifs. Celebrates the machine age while keeping craftsman-grade detail.

name: Art Nouveau
description: Whiplash curves, plant-form ornament, integrated decorative arts, wrought iron. Organic opposition to academic classicism.

name: Bauhaus
description: Proto-modernist unity of art, craft, and industry. Rational, unadorned volumes, primary colors as accents, flat roofs, ribbon windows.

name: International Style
description: Le Corbusier's five points made global: pilotis, free plan, free facade, horizontal windows, roof garden. Machine-smooth, unornamented volumes.

name: Brutalism
description: Béton brut (raw concrete) expressed as form and texture. Sculptural massing, heavy overhangs, deep shadow, programmatic honesty.

name: Modernist
description: Form-follows-function orthodoxy. Steel frame, glass curtain walls, open plans, machine aesthetic. Umbrella style for mid-century rationalism.

name: Postmodern
description: Ironic reintroduction of historical ornament, color, and symbol. Rejects modernist purism in favor of pluralism and wit.

name: Deconstructivism
description: Fragmented, non-rectilinear forms; collisions of volumes; studied visual instability. Gehry, Hadid, Libeskind.

name: Parametric
description: Algorithm-driven continuous surfaces, smooth curves, biomimetic geometry. Hadid, Foster, MAD.

name: High-Tech
description: Structure and services externalized as ornament. Color-coded ducts, exposed trusses, glass skin. Piano, Rogers, Foster.

name: Craftsman / Arts & Crafts
description: Reaction against industrial decoration — hand-made joinery, low-pitched gables, deep eaves, natural materials, exposed rafters.

name: Prairie School
description: Frank Lloyd Wright's low, horizontal homes with deep eaves, banded windows, and central hearth. Integrated with the flat landscape.

name: Victorian
description: Umbrella for ornate 19th-century styles (Italianate, Queen Anne, Second Empire). Steep roofs, asymmetric plans, turrets, elaborate trim.

name: Tudor Revival
description: Half-timbered walls, steep gables, tall mullioned windows, prominent chimneys. Revival versions emphasize medieval romance.

name: Palladian
description: Andrea Palladio's codified classicism: symmetric plans, temple-front porticoes, perfect-ratio rooms. Foundation of Western classical revival.

name: American Colonial
description: Symmetric, boxy homes with central entries, multi-pane sash windows, side-gabled roofs. Pragmatic, restrained.

name: Moorish / Islamic Spain
description: Horseshoe arches, muqarnas (stalactite vaulting), geometric tilework, central courtyards with fountains. Alhambra is the exemplar.

name: Ottoman
description: Large central dome supported by half-domes, pencil-thin minarets, broad prayer halls. Sinan's mosques are the canon.

name: Mughal
description: Fusion of Persian, Indian, and Islamic traditions: onion domes, four-iwan plans, chhatris, red sandstone and white marble. Taj Mahal is the apex.

name: Japanese Traditional
description: Post-and-beam timber with deep hipped roofs, sliding shoji screens, engawa verandas. Structure expressed; ornament restrained.

name: Chinese Imperial
description: Symmetric palace compounds with upturned hipped roofs, vermilion walls, golden tiles, dougong bracketing, axial ceremonial routes.

name: Mesoamerican
description: Stepped stone pyramids with temples atop, ritual ball courts, carved glyphs, monumental plazas. Maya and Aztec variants.

name: Ancient Egyptian
description: Massive stone masses, battered walls, hypostyle halls, lotus and papyrus capitals, hieroglyph-covered surfaces. Designed for permanence.

name: Classical Greek
description: Trabeated temples with columns, entablature, and pediment. The orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian) codify proportion.

name: Classical Roman
description: Trabeated-plus-arcuated hybrid enabled by concrete. Arches, vaults, domes at monumental scale. Basilica, thermae, forum typologies.

name: Alpine Vernacular
description: Timber chalets with steep shed roofs, carved balconies, and deep stone bases. Adapted to snow load and cold winters.

name: Mediterranean Vernacular
description: Whitewashed stone or stucco walls, terracotta tile roofs, small shaded openings, courtyards. Adapted to heat and sun.

name: Adobe / Pueblo
description: Sun-dried mud brick walls with rounded corners, flat roofs with projecting viga beams, small deep windows. Thermal mass for desert climate.

name: Scandinavian Stave
description: All-timber churches with steeply stacked tiered roofs, dragon-head finials, intricate post-and-beam framing. Viking craft applied to Christian program.

name: Russian Orthodox
description: Onion-domed churches, kokoshnik gables, brightly colored tiled roofs, cross-in-square plans. St Basil's is the icon.

name: Pointed Arch
description: Two arcs meeting at an apex. Directs thrust downward more efficiently than semicircular arches, enabling taller openings and thinner walls.

name: Semicircular (Round) Arch
description: Half-circle arch distributing load through voussoirs to springings. Foundation of Roman and Romanesque construction.

name: Ogee Arch
description: S-curve arch with an inflection — concave at base, convex to apex. Decorative rather than structural; common in windows and niches.

name: Horseshoe Arch
description: Arch whose curve extends past a semicircle, giving a flared horseshoe shape. Signature of Islamic architecture in Spain.

name: Flying Buttress
description: External half-arch that carries the outward thrust of a nave vault across an aisle to a stout pier buttress. Frees the nave wall for windows.

name: Rib Vault
description: Groin vault with reinforcing stone ribs along the arris. Ribs are built first and carry the web panels, reducing centering and weight.

name: Barrel Vault
description: Continuous semicircular vault extruded along one axis. Simple and heavy; requires thick supporting walls.

name: Groin Vault
description: Intersection of two barrel vaults at right angles creating four webs divided by diagonal groins. Lighter than barrel; concentrates load on corners.

name: Dome on Pendentives
description: Hemispherical dome supported on triangular spherical-pendentive transitions that mediate between a circular dome base and a square bay.

name: Oculus
description: Circular opening at the apex of a dome or wall. The Pantheon's oculus is 8.7m wide.

name: Clerestory
description: Upper row of windows above aisle roofs admitting light into a tall central nave. Defines the basilican section.

name: Rose Window
description: Large circular window with radial tracery, typically above a cathedral's west portal or transept ends. Wheel-like stained glass composition.

name: Tracery
description: Stonework mullions dividing a window into ornamental patterns. Evolves from plate tracery through bar tracery to Perpendicular.

name: Pier Buttress
description: Solid masonry pile projecting from a wall to resist lateral thrust. Used alone in Romanesque, paired with flyers in Gothic.

name: Doric Column
description: Stoutest of the Greek orders: no base, fluted shaft, plain echinus-abacus capital. Symbol of strength.

name: Ionic Column
description: Slender with volute capital and molded base. Associated with grace and the feminine; often in interior colonnades.

name: Corinthian Column
description: Most ornate order: bell-shaped capital wreathed with acanthus leaves. Roman architects elaborated it further.

name: Solomonic Column
description: Twisted-spiral shaft evoking Solomon's Temple. Bernini's baldacchino in St Peter's popularized its baroque use.

name: Pediment
description: Triangular gable above an entablature, often sculpted. Variants: broken, segmental, swan-neck, open-bed.

name: Cornice
description: Projecting crown moulding that sheds rainwater away from a wall and caps the entablature. Rich profile possibilities.

name: Entablature
description: Horizontal superstructure carried on columns: architrave (bottom), frieze (middle), cornice (top). Order-specific proportions.

name: Pilaster
description: Rectangular column engaged in a wall, carrying capital and base like a full column. Structural or purely ornamental.

name: Dome
description: Hemispherical or pointed vault centered on a single axis. From Pantheon's concrete shell to Brunelleschi's double dome to Buckminster Fuller's geodesics.

name: Spire
description: Tall pointed termination of a tower. Structural challenge — Salisbury's 123m is among the medieval record holders.

name: Minaret
description: Slender tower from which the call to prayer is given. Regional variants: pencil-thin (Ottoman), square (Maghreb), spiral (Samarra).

name: Pagoda Tier
description: Stacked tiered roof level of a pagoda; each storey slightly smaller than the one below, eaves curving upward.

name: Chhatri
description: Elevated, dome-shaped pavilion on slim pillars. Marks rooflines and corners of Mughal and Rajput buildings.

name: Onion Dome
description: Bulbous dome whose diameter exceeds its drum, rising to a point. Iconic silhouette.

name: Crenellation
description: Parapet with alternating merlons and crenels (solid blocks and gaps) for archers and aesthetic military expression.

name: Machicolation
description: Projecting gallery along a fortification top with openings in the floor for dropping stones or boiling oil on attackers at the base.

name: Gargoyle
description: Carved waterspout projecting from a cornice to throw rain clear of walls. Often zoomorphic or grotesque.

name: Keystone
description: Central wedge-shaped voussoir at the apex of an arch. Structurally holds the arch together; often emphasized decoratively.

name: Rustication
description: Masonry technique: rough-faced blocks with pronounced recessed joints. Usually on basements to imply strength.

name: Portico
description: Covered porch of columns supporting a pediment or entablature. Temple front transferred to civic and domestic use.

name: Palladian Window
description: Three-part window with a central arched light flanked by two narrower rectangular lights. Signature motif of Palladianism.

name: Bay Window
description: Window projecting outward from a wall in faceted or curved form. Increases light and interior floor area.

name: Clerestory Window
description: High window band just below a roof, above eye level. Used in Egyptian hypostyle halls, Gothic naves, modernist lofts alike.

name: Mullion
description: Vertical bar dividing a window into lights. Stone in Gothic, timber in domestic, steel in modernist curtain walls.

name: Battlement
description: Parapet with crenellation along the top of a wall or tower. Defensive origin, decorative later.

name: Arcade
description: A row of arches carried on columns or piers. Can be structural (aqueduct, cloister) or decorative (blind arcade).

name: Loggia
description: Gallery or corridor open on one side via columns or piers, often overlooking a courtyard or landscape.

name: Atrium
description: Central open or glazed space inside a building receiving daylight. Roman domestic version open to sky; modern version glazed.

name: Apse
description: Semicircular or polygonal recess at the end of a basilica or church, typically housing the altar or magistrate's seat.

name: Transept
description: Cross-axis arm of a cruciform church, intersecting the nave. Forms the transverse of the Latin cross.

name: Nave
description: Long central aisle of a basilican church, running from the west front to the crossing or chancel. Holds the congregation.

name: Aisle
description: Passageway flanking the nave of a basilica, separated by an arcade. Supports lower roof that lets clerestory windows above.

name: Cloister
description: Square garden enclosed by a covered arcade on all four sides, central to monastic plan. Place for meditation and circulation.

name: Belfry / Bell Tower
description: Tower housing bells, either integrated with a church (campanile) or freestanding. Italian Romanesque variants are iconic.

name: Stained Glass
description: Pieces of colored glass assembled with lead cames in large window tracery. Tells biblical narrative and colors interior light.

name: Grand Staircase
description: Ceremonial stair as an architectural centerpiece — imperial, scissored, or curving around a central void.

name: Corbel
description: Projecting stone or timber bracket carrying weight from a beam, balcony, or parapet. Often carved decoratively.

name: Cantilever
description: Beam or slab fixed at one end only, projecting into space. Enabled by reinforced concrete and steel — Fallingwater's signature.

name: Diagrid Structure
description: Diagonal grid of steel members that carries both gravity and lateral loads without a vertical column grid. Used in the Gherkin, Hearst Tower.

name: Curtain Wall
description: Non-load-bearing outer skin hung from the structural frame. Glass and aluminum systems dominate postwar office towers.

name: Pilotis
description: Ground-level columns lifting a building's mass into the air, freeing the ground plane. Le Corbusier's first point.

name: Gable Roof
description: Two sloped planes meeting at a ridge with triangular gable walls at each end. Most common pitched roof form.

name: Hip Roof
description: Roof sloping on all four sides. Wind-resistant and compact. Pyramidal if square plan.

name: Mansard Roof
description: Double-pitched roof with a near-vertical lower slope pierced by dormers, and a shallow upper slope. Named after François Mansart.

name: Dormer
description: Roofed projection containing a window on a sloped roof. Gives attic space natural light.

name: Jali
description: Perforated stone screen with lattice patterns. Filters light, reduces glare, and provides privacy while admitting breezes.

name: Muqarnas
description: Honeycomb of prismatic niches cascading down a vault or transition zone. Stalactite-like, ornamental.

name: Iwan
description: Vaulted hall open at one end, framed by a portal (pishtaq). Four-iwan plan surrounds a courtyard.

name: Pishtaq
description: Rectangular frame surrounding the arched portal of an iwan. Often taller than the main facade to heighten the entrance.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
description: Early Gothic cathedral with influential rose windows, flying buttresses added mid-construction, and a 69m central spire (Viollet-le-Duc, lost 2019).

name: Chartres Cathedral
description: High Gothic paradigm — most of its 172 stained glass windows survive intact. Asymmetric twin spires and flying buttresses with pointed arcade.

name: Reims Cathedral
description: Coronation church of French kings. Facade features over 2300 sculpted figures; extensive flying buttress system.

name: Cologne Cathedral
description: Largest Gothic cathedral by facade — 157m twin spires make it Europe's third-tallest cathedral. Built over 632 years.

name: Milan Cathedral (Duomo)
description: Largest Gothic cathedral in Italy, roof bristling with 135 spires and over 3400 statues. White Candoglia marble.

name: Westminster Abbey
description: English Gothic royal church, coronation site, with tallest English nave (31m) and fan-vaulted Henry VII Chapel.

name: Salisbury Cathedral
description: English Early Gothic in 38 years — unusual unified construction. Tallest medieval spire in the UK at 123m.

name: Sagrada Família
description: Gaudí's masterwork of organic geometry: hyperboloid vaults, parabolic arches, tree-like branching columns. 18 planned spires up to 172m.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: Justinian's masterwork — central dome 31m span on pendentives, 56m tall at apex. Defined Byzantine architecture for 1000 years.

name: Sultan Ahmed (Blue) Mosque
description: Five main domes cascading down from 43m central dome, six minarets, interior clad in ~20,000 blue Iznik tiles.

name: Taj Mahal
description: White marble mausoleum on a red sandstone plinth, flanked by four minarets and preceded by a formal charbagh garden with reflecting pool.

name: Alhambra
description: Nasrid palace complex with courtyards — Lions, Myrtles — muqarnas vaults, and intricate geometric tilework.

name: Great Mosque of Córdoba
description: Hypostyle prayer hall with 856 jasper, onyx, marble, and granite columns carrying two-tier red-and-white striped horseshoe arches.

name: Pantheon (Rome)
description: Largest unreinforced concrete dome ever — 43.3m span with a 9m oculus. Rotunda diameter equals height, producing a perfect sphere.

name: Parthenon
description: Doric temple of Athena with 46 outer columns, optical refinements (entasis, stylobate curvature), and marble frieze.

name: Colosseum
description: Elliptical amphitheater holding 50,000. Four superimposed orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, pilasters) in an 80-bay arcade.

name: Villa Rotonda
description: Palladio's central-plan villa with a Greek cross plan, four identical Ionic porticoes, and a central dome. Template for countless imitations.

name: St Peter's Basilica
description: Largest church in the world. Michelangelo's double-shell 42m dome crowns a Greek cross plan elongated by Maderno into a Latin cross.

name: Florence Duomo
description: Brunelleschi's double-shell brick dome spans 45m without centering — engineering breakthrough that opened the Renaissance.

name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
description: Nine polychrome onion-domed chapels around a central tent roof. Commemorates Ivan IV's conquest of Kazan.

name: Fallingwater
description: Wright's cantilevered reinforced-concrete terraces project over Bear Run waterfall. Integrates masonry and landscape.

name: Villa Savoye
description: Le Corbusier's embodiment of the Five Points: pilotis, free plan, free facade, ribbon window, roof garden. White prism on slender columns.

name: Barcelona Pavilion
description: Mies van der Rohe's horizontal platform with free-standing marble walls, eight chromed cruciform columns, and reflecting pool.

name: Farnsworth House
description: Mies's 'less-is-more' glass box: 8 white-painted steel columns lifting a floating slab. Entirely transparent envelope.

name: Guggenheim Bilbao
description: Gehry's titanium-clad curves conceived in CATIA. Catalyst of the 'Bilbao effect' for cultural architecture.

name: Sydney Opera House
description: Utzon's spherical-geometry shells clad in 1.056 million Swedish tiles. Precedent-setting computational geometry.

name: Centre Pompidou
description: Piano & Rogers's inside-out museum: color-coded services (blue ducts, red circulation, green plumbing, yellow electrical) on the facade.

name: Louvre Pyramid
description: I.M. Pei's 21.6m glass pyramid marks the Louvre's main entrance. 603 rhombus + 70 triangular laminated glass panes.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: 828m tallest building. Y-shaped buttressed core with three setback wings reducing wind vortex shedding.

name: The Shard
description: Renzo Piano's 310m tapered glass pyramid. Irregular sloped-glass facets converge toward a 'shattered' top.

name: CCTV Headquarters
description: OMA's continuous-loop tower: two leaning towers joined at top by a cantilevered overhang and at bottom by a plinth. Structural diagrid skin.

name: Empire State Building
description: Art Deco skyscraper 443m tall with stepped setbacks, stainless-steel mooring mast, and limestone facade.

name: Chrysler Building
description: Van Alen's stainless-steel sunburst crown rises in seven radiating arches. Eagles and radiator-cap gargoyles reference car culture.

name: Seagram Building
description: Mies's bronze-and-glass tower set back on an elevated plaza — the template for corporate modernism worldwide.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
description: Wright's continuous spiral ramp winds around a central atrium. Inverted ziggurat form in poured concrete.

name: Unité d'Habitation
description: Le Corbusier's 337-apartment concrete megastructure on massive pilotis. Interior 'street' and roof gymnasium define the type.

name: Notre-Dame-du-Haut (Ronchamp)
description: Le Corbusier's pilgrimage chapel with a curving concrete boat-keel roof and deep irregular window apertures. A break from his rationalism.

name: Robie House
description: Wright's prairie masterpiece: horizontal brick bands, 6m cantilevered eaves, and a central hearth in cruciform plan.

name: Monticello
description: Jefferson's own home: Palladian villa adapted to Virginia climate with octagonal dome, Doric portico, and integral dependencies.

name: Angkor Wat
description: Largest religious structure by area. Five lotus-bud towers on a pyramidal temple mount symbolizing Mount Meru. Originally Vishnu, later Buddhist.

name: Borobudur
description: Nine stacked platforms — six square, three circular — crowned by a central stupa. 504 Buddha statues and 2672 relief panels.

name: Forbidden City
description: Ming-Qing palace complex of 980 buildings on 72ha. Axial courtyards, yellow-tiled hipped roofs, vermilion walls.

name: Himeji Castle
description: White Heron Castle — six-level dondjon, brilliant white plaster walls, upturned curved gables, on a fortified stone base.

name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Three-storey pavilion: upper two clad in gold leaf, crowned by a bronze phoenix. Each floor a different style (shinden, samurai, zen).

name: Hōryū-ji Pagoda
description: Oldest wooden building on Earth. Five-storey pagoda with central post (shinbashira) that dampens earthquakes.

name: Machu Picchu
description: Stone citadel on a saddle at 2430m between peaks. Dry-laid ashlar masonry, terraced agricultural plots, ritual observatories.

name: Chichén Itzá (El Castillo)
description: Step pyramid of Kukulkan. 91 steps on each of four sides + top platform = 365, matching the solar year.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Khufu's pyramid — 146m at completion, 6.5M tonnes of limestone. Aligned to true north within 4 arc-minutes.

name: Karnak Temple Complex
description: Vast religious complex; its Great Hypostyle Hall has 134 columns up to 21m tall, papyrus-capitaled.

name: Al-Khazneh (Petra Treasury)
description: Rock-cut 40m facade carved into sandstone cliff. Tholos with broken pediment flanked by split triangular pediments.

name: Tempio Malatestiano
description: Alberti's transformation of a Gothic church with a triple triumphal-arch facade based on the Arch of Augustus.

name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
description: Hemispherical solid stupa surrounded by a circumambulatory path, enclosed by a stone railing with four monumental toranas (gateways).

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
description: 99m gold-plated stupa on a raised terrace surrounded by 100+ smaller shrines. Crown inlaid with ~7000 diamonds.

name: Great Wall of China
description: Series of fortifications totaling ~21000km. Ming-era rammed earth and brick walls 6–8m high with watchtowers every 150–500m.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
description: World's largest mud-brick building. Three minarets, palm-log toron projections for re-plastering, adobe walls.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: Ludwig II's fantasy castle — Romanesque Revival silhouette crowned with fairy-tale spires and towers, perched on a crag.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: Louis XIV's residence: Hall of Mirrors 73m long, formal gardens extending to 8.2km axis. Symbol of absolutism.

name: Mont Saint-Michel Abbey
description: Benedictine abbey on a tidal-island granite mount rising 80m. Multiple construction phases fuse Romanesque base with Flamboyant Gothic apex.

name: St Pancras Station
description: Gilbert Scott's red-brick Gothic Revival hotel fronting Barlow's 74m single-span iron train shed — largest in the world at opening.

name: Crystal Palace
description: Paxton's 563m prefabricated iron-and-glass exhibition hall for the Great Exhibition. Proto-modernist, assembled in 22 weeks.

name: Eiffel Tower
description: 330m wrought-iron lattice tower of 18038 parts, 2.5M rivets. Graceful parabolic curve optimized for wind load.

name: Petronas Twin Towers
description: 452m twin towers linked by a 58m skybridge at the 41st floor. Plan geometry derives from the Islamic eight-pointed star.

name: 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin)
description: Foster's 180m curvilinear tower with a diagrid skin and spiraling light wells for natural ventilation.

name: Marina Bay Sands
description: Three 55-storey towers joined by a 340m SkyPark cantilevering 67m beyond the easternmost tower. Cantilevered resort deck.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Jean Nouvel's 180m-wide double-layer steel dome of 7850 stars. Produces a 'rain of light' filtering through 8 cladding layers.

name: Therme Vals
description: Zumthor's monolithic thermal baths — 60,000 slabs of local Valser quartzite stacked like sedimentary strata.

name: Kimbell Art Museum
description: Louis Kahn's parallel cycloid-vaulted bays with continuous skylight slits reflecting light off diffusing baffles.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
description: Niemeyer's crown-of-thorns — 16 hyperbolic concrete columns curving upward to support a glass roof over a sunken nave.

name: Erechtheion
description: Ionic temple on the Acropolis with the Caryatid Porch — six sculpted female figures in place of columns.

name: Liaodi Pagoda
description: Tallest existing brick pagoda in China — 84m, 13 storeys of octagonal masonry with decorative corbelled eaves.

name: Pyramid of the Sun (Teotihuacán)
description: Third-largest pyramid in the world by volume. Talud-tablero slope composed of rubble core with stucco cladding.

name: Kailasa Temple (Ellora)
description: World's largest monolithic rock-cut structure — carved top-down from a single basalt cliff, estimated 200,000 tonnes of stone removed.

name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
description: Gaudí's undulating stone facade with wrought-iron balconies, and a rooftop of chimneys disguised as helmeted warriors.

name: Casa Batlló
description: Gaudí remodel with skull-like balconies, dragon-back roof of colored ceramic scales, bone-shaped columns.

name: Hungarian Parliament Building
description: One of the largest legislative buildings — 268m long Danube-facing facade with 365 spires and a central Gothic Revival dome.

name: Moscow Kremlin
description: Fortified citadel with red-brick walls (2235m long), 20 towers, containing cathedrals and palaces. Italian Renaissance architects contributed the walls.

name: Basilica of Aquileia
description: Early Christian basilica with an enormous 4th-century floor mosaic (760 m²) depicting Jonah cycle and marine fauna.

name: Court of the Lions
description: Central courtyard of the Nasrid Palaces: 124 slim marble columns arcading a rectangular courtyard around a fountain on twelve lion sculptures.

name: Oslo Opera House
description: Snøhetta's 'walkable roof' of Italian marble that rises from the harbor as a sloping public plaza. 18000 m² of La Facciata marble.

name: Hearst Tower
description: Foster's 46-storey diagrid tower rising from the stone base of the 1928 Hearst Magazine Building. 20% less steel than a conventional frame.

name: Thomas Jefferson Library (UVA)
description: Jefferson's Rotunda references the Pantheon at half-scale: brick shell, Corinthian portico, copper dome. Anchors the Academical Village.

name: Louvre (Cour Carrée)
description: Square courtyard of the Louvre rebuilt by Lescot — introduced classical orders to French palace design. Crowned by sculpted attic.

name: Charles Bridge
description: 516m stone arch bridge over the Vltava. 16 sandstone arches, 30 baroque statues added in the 17th–18th centuries.

name: Dancing House (Prague)
description: Gehry & Milunić's playful pair of towers leaning into each other as dancers ('Fred and Ginger'), 99 uniquely shaped concrete panels.

name: Cité de Carcassonne
description: Double-walled medieval city with 52 towers, restored by Viollet-le-Duc. Inner wall late Roman, outer 13th-century with machicolations.

name: Tōdai-ji Daibutsuden
description: One of the world's largest wooden buildings, housing the 15m Great Buddha. Hipped-and-gabled roof with bronze shibi ornaments.

name: Tikal (Temple IV)
description: Tallest pre-Columbian structure in the Americas — 70m roof comb rising above jungle canopy. Nine-stepped pyramidal base.

name: Villa Müller
description: Adolf Loos's manifesto of Raumplan — volumes of differing heights interlocked in three dimensions. Stripped external geometry, rich interior materials.
